finding.issue: The supposedly loaded inspector is obtained from admission.inspectCanonicalSource inside each factory call. The immediate own-value identity check therefore compares a possibly already-replaced property to itself. The source text digest does not authenticate its lexical closure.
finding.concrete_counterexample: The actual genuine legacy and table CJS inspectCanonicalSource function bodies are byte-for-byte identical 370 bytes and both hash to 619ce1daf34bc76fa9e610af6e28496957094b4ff4c5d14eb492664405cd67ca, but close over different SHA and inspectSource. Replace the legacy export with the genuine table function before calling composeSourceGuards:true: the cold entry check accepts it, tools and subsequent reads invoke supplied callbacks, and the wrong inspector is eventually invoked. Its different SHA is expected to reject there, so no incorrect positive is asserted; the cold identity/zero-callback and no-redirect invariant is nonetheless violated.
finding.fix: Capture the actual legacy inspector at module initialization under trusted committed startup, then compare own-data property identity to that capture and digest before supplied callbacks and at final. Add real cold swapped-identical-body test and late pointer/accessor tests; verify no supplied callback and no swapped inspector call on cold rejection.
